Hey Jordan / team - looping in some technical details so we can hit the ground running at the deep-dive. High level: we support three control-plane patterns relevant to your requirements:

1) Managed control plane (hosted by Redwood): easiest to operate; requires TLS outbound to our control endpoints (not ideal for air-gap).
2) Customer-managed control plane (recommended for AcmeHealth): control plane services run in your VPC/DMZ. No control-plane egress is required; boarding & upgrades can be done over an administrative channel you control (VPN or temporary bastion).
3) Fully air-gapped on-prem (for highest isolation): the entire control plane + serving runtime runs behind your perimeter. We ship an installer and playbooks; package includes audit logging integration and KMS/HSM connectors (requires a small bootstrap channel for license/attestation, or can be done offline with signed manifests).

Competitive notes vs hyperscaler offering:
- Hyperscaler managed private endpoints typically trade off telem/ops convenience for egress and telemetry (their managed control plane keeps a persistent channel). That's often the blocker for regulated customers.
- Performance: our runtime uses continuous batching and KV-cache sharing that often yields better cost/throughput for conversational workloads vs single-tenant hyperscaler endpoints; we included a short matrix (redwood-vs-hyperscaler-matrix.xlsx) with latency/throughput profiles from earlier POCs.

Suggested POC tests and acceptance criteria:
- Connectivity test: validate that control plane can be installed in your VPC with zero outbound to public internet. Criteria: config and health APIs reachable from private subnets only.
- Functional test: load a 1GB model, run 50 concurrent streams at 512-token gen for 15 min, measure 95p latency and tokens/sec.
- Resilience test: simulate node drain and validate KV cache warm-up time and steady-state latency.

Attachments: redwood-vs-hyperscaler-matrix.xlsx (benchmark summary), internal SE checklist (we'll share during call).

I'll be on the deep-dive and can walk through deployment options and the air-gap playbook.
